title: Log-domain Lyapunov core-tail drift corridor
question: Can a logarithmic Lyapunov drift outside a high-probability core replace a pointwise conditional-mass floor, while a core intrinsic gap and boundary rate provide a finite corridor toward a common-core estimate?

new_perspective.principle: Treat small conditional masses as a tail to be controlled by a Foster-Lyapunov drift, not by a uniform pointwise floor. Combine the tail drift with the induced core graph gap and the core-to-tail jump rate before asking for a global Poincare or Schur bound.
route: Reconstruct Gibbs and conditional rows in the R-416 log domain and define phi_i=log(pi_max)-log(pi_i).
For alpha>0 set V_i=exp(alpha phi_i) and use the reversible conductance generator Lf(i)=sum_j c_ij(f_j-f_i)/pi_i; record kappa_tail=min_{phi_i>=theta}[-LV(i)/V_i].
Define the core K_theta={phi<theta}, compute its induced projected graph gap, its mass and the maximum core-to-tail jump rate, and retain tail mass as a separate error budget.
Stress alpha, theta, cutoff, beta and both collar orientations, then compare independent reconstructions without promoting any observed envelope.
Use hostile sign, inverse-potential, disconnected-core and zero-mass mutations so drift direction, core connectivity and positivity remain load-bearing.
new_perspective.qft_bridge: A successful analytic route would prove uniform tail drift, core gap, boundary-rate and observable-tail estimates on one Hamiltonian common core, then derive an explicit Lyapunov-Poincare/Schur inequality and transfer it to R-399/R-415. The finite corridor only identifies the constants and the missing theorem.

finite_theorem.generator: For positive pi and symmetric conductance c, Lf(i)=pi_i^(-1) sum_j c_ij(f_j-f_i).
finite_theorem.lyapunov: If V_i>0 and kappa_tail=min_{i in T_theta}[-LV(i)/V_i]>0, then LV<=-kappa_tail V on the finite tail T_theta by direct substitution.
finite_theorem.core: The induced core graph uses c restricted to K_theta and rescaled by the core mass; its projected first positive eigenvalue is a finite conditional gap diagnostic.
finite_theorem.corridor: Tail mass, tail drift, core gap and core-to-tail jump rate are recorded together. A global Poincare inequality would additionally require an analytic variance decomposition and uniform control of the tail observable term.
finite_theorem.scope: The calculation is finite and numerical. It does not assert a uniform Lyapunov inequality, a global Poincare constant, a common Hamiltonian core, a GNS gap or a QFT mass gap.

lean_crosscheck.boundary: Lean checks only scalar sign, positivity and finite-scope bookkeeping; the matrix generator, log-domain Gibbs law, core spectrum, tail estimate and all uniform/QFT limits remain executable/open analysis.

promotion_criteria: Prove a cutoff-, volume-, phase- and exhaustion-uniform drift inequality for one source-independent Lyapunov potential on the Hamiltonian common core.
Prove a uniform induced-core Schur/Poincare gap and a boundary-rate estimate, including the neutral and inter-phase capacities.
Control the tail contribution for the actual R-399 likelihood observables in the same two-sided form norm and transfer the result through R-415 before revisiting GNS coercivity.
stop_conditions: If the tail drift changes sign, the core disconnects or the tail mass is not controlled on a growing stress, retain the corridor as a diagnostic and redesign the potential or the core partition.
If independent or hostile checks disagree, stop promotion and repair the generator normalization, log convention or induced-core scaling before interpreting any gap.
A finite positive drift and core gap do not prove a global Poincare inequality, a common core, a GNS gap, a continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite log-domain Lyapunov core-tail corridor only. It proves no cutoff-, volume-, source-, phase- or exhaustion-uniform drift, no global Poincare or Schur theorem, no common Hamiltonian core, no OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, no physical mass gap, no continuum, no C6, no Sector-A and no Pre-A closure.
no_overclaim: The new perspective replaces a fragile pointwise floor by an auditable tail-drift/core-gap interface. Its finite persistence is a route discriminator and a list of analytic debts, not regulator-independent coercivity.
